question: Should OpenClaw adopt this private 22-locale core package and 15-surface coverage manifest now as the canonical localization contract before later runtime and plugin slices proceed?
rationale: The patch establishes long-lived package, locale, coverage, fallback, and CI policy across product owners; code review cannot infer that architecture from the open RFC and protected maintainer signal.

options.title: Approve the foundation
options.body: Confirm the RFC boundary, authorize the internal dependency graph, and require live upgrade and fresh-install proof before landing the package and its two initial consumers.

options.title: Narrow the extraction
options.body: Share only locale normalization and direction metadata now, leaving catalogs and cross-surface coverage policy until RFC owners agree on lifecycle and ownership.

options.title: Pause for RFC completion
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer landing until RFC 0024 resolves package ownership, supported locales, plugin participation, and coverage governance.

recommendation.title: Approve the foundation
recommendation.body: Confirm the RFC boundary, authorize the internal dependency graph, and require live upgrade and fresh-install proof before landing the package and its two initial consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is the Control UI locale sync pipeline and registry expansion this proposal would replace and generalize.
